title: StylePack
description: Behavior document, consumed by the PLANNER and the COMPILER. Pacing numbers are constraints, not advice.

video_type.description: the video-type preset this pack implements; a channel's video_type picks among packs. Same enum as channel_config.video_type

hold_floor_ratio.description: post-alignment per-beat FLOOR, as a multiple of min_hold. Narration beat durations are emergent from SRT alignment and never checked, so a beat can land at 0.8s and flash by; the compiler merges any visual slot below min_hold * this into its neighbour. 0 disables the pass — the schema default, so a video enqueued before this field existed re-runs byte-identically (Principle 7). The shipped packs set 1.0.

hold_ceiling_ratio.description: post-alignment per-beat CEILING, as a multiple of max_hold. A slot holding one long sentence has no boundary to cut at and sits there dead; the compiler divides anything above max_hold * this into equal slots. 0 disables the pass (see hold_floor_ratio). The shipped packs set 1.5.

hook.description: D106 — the opening hook, from the start of the narration to subjects.json hook_end_cut (a pipeline without the subjects stage has no hook to pace). Dark Palace's hook: faster cuts on word onsets, opening on footage, closing on the video's title with a riser into a hit. Off unless enabled, so a pack that does not set it compiles exactly as before.

mode.description: D107 — Dark Palace's hook option. classic = footage and the pack's own overlays; headlines = the hook_plan stage also puts 2-5 moments of the hook on screen in varied forms (a headline in big type, one giant word, a marked phrase of the narration, two number cards), each landing on words the narration says and never showing a number it does not.

cut_s.description: target seconds per hook shot; each cut moves to the nearest word onset

min_hold.description: the hook's own hold floor, in place of pacing.min_hold x hold_floor_ratio

max_share.description: the hook never runs longer than this share of the narration: a later hook_end_cut is pulled back to the last cut that fits

open_on.description: footage = no graphic covers the first shot, and that shot is video rather than a still

component.description: catalog component whose `text` prop takes the video's title

lead_cue.description: sound-pack cue leading into the card (its lead_s pulls it earlier)

hit_cue.description: sound-pack cue on the card's entrance

rhythm.description: D113 — the body's rhythm after the hook (Dark Palace's montar): about one shot per shot_s, no planned still past max_still_s, cuts on a spoken word, never two panel graphics in a row. Every knob is off by default, so a pack without the block compiles exactly as before. The hook keeps its own pacing (pacing.hook).

shot_s.description: a shot longer than this becomes ceil(duration / shot_s) equal shots. 0 = off. DP: 5 (one 15 s take read as stuck)

max_still_s.description: the same for a shot the plan puts a photo on. 0 = off. DP: 6

snap_to_words.description: a cut inside a beat (the hold ceiling's and these) moves to the nearest word onset within 0.5 s, leaving no shot under 1 s

min_graphic_gap_s.description: after the hook, a panel graphic (one filling half the frame's height or more) that starts less than this after the previous one ended is dropped, and the earlier one keeps the moment. Corner tags never count. 0 = off

allowed_packs.description: component packs the planner may draw from — the menu filter AND the validate rule (belt and suspenders). Pack granularity, not per component: a channel resolves to `core` plus at most one installed pack (packs are additive), so this says which EXTRA packs a style suits. `core` is always in the menu and listing it here is redundant; omitting it does not remove it. Omitted means every pack. Per-component trimming is the channel's job, via look.exclude.components.

emphasis.description: D59 — a SECOND overlay class, keyed on where attention needs a lift rather than on a fact in the script. Off by default: `density` above is anchor-gated, so it tracks factual density, which is right for a documentary and limiting for a faster channel. The two classes are counted under separate budgets, so turning this on cannot dilute the first.

per_minute.description: ceiling for emphasis overlays alone, per minute of narration

mix.description: D114 — mastering. Omitted = the D48 mix: everything summed, then one single-pass loudnorm to -14 LUFS on the bus.

voice_lufs.description: the narration is normalized to this (two-pass, linear) before anything is mixed against it (Dark Palace: -14)

master.description: the finished mix's loudness pass to -14 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP: single = one dynamic pass (D48); two_pass = measure, then one linear gain, so the balance of voice, bed and cues is kept as mixed

captions.description: D113 — how the narration is cut into captions. Whether captions show at all, and where, is the channel's (channel_config.captions).

chunk.description: short phrases shown from their first spoken word (Dark Palace's _frases): a phrase ends at max_chars or max_words, after . ? ! and after , ; : once it has four words; a tail under ten characters joins the phrase before it. Omitted = one caption per narration timing chunk, as before.

texture.description: D112 — WHERE the film texture lands (Dark Palace's DG_EFEITOS). The theme's `texture` says what it looks like. `narrative` reads marks.json (the narrative_marks stage): a light leak on the cut into each story turn, the vintage grade over flashback passages, an old CRT set on the first footage of each flashback. `count` is the fixed rhythm for a script with no story shape: a leak every `leak_every`th picture cut, the grade on every `vintage_every`th shot. `off` (the default) places nothing, so a pack without this block compiles byte-identically.

light_leak.description: false keeps the grade and the CRT set but places no light leak; a channel's look.exclude.transitions naming light_leak sets it

leak_min_gap_s.description: two light leaks never land closer than this

vintage_max_share.description: the grade never covers more than this share of the picture shots

leak_every.description: count mode: every Nth picture cut gets a leak

vintage_every.description: count mode: every Nth shot after the hook is aged

duration_s.description: D89 — how long a non-cut transition runs. The PACK owns this, not the beat: a transition eats footage from the shots on both sides of it, so its length is a property of the style's pacing, not of one junction. Omitted means 0.5s, which is what every transition was before. The compiler clamps it against both neighbours and degrades to a cut when a beat is too short to give it room.

animated_share.description: D95 — the target share of junctions that are NOT a cut, e.g. 0.3 for a 70/30 mix. The compiler places them: section breaks first, then FILLER from `mix`, spread evenly, never two animated junctions side by side. A target, not a promise: a junction whose shots are too short to hold the transition stays a cut, so a fast pack delivers less than it asks (the compile note says how much). Omitted means no filler — every junction is the default, as before. Capped at 0.6 because past that a mix stops being a mix. Requires `mix`.

mix.description: D95 — which kinds FILLER draws from, as relative weights ({"crossfade": 2, "fade_to_black": 1} is two crossfades per dip). Each kind must be in `allowed`. The kind at a junction is picked from a hash of the shot's id, so a recompile of the same beats picks the same kinds. Read only when `animated_share` is set.

section_break.description: D95 — the transition where the story changes section. The signal is the MUSIC's: a section starts where the mood span changes (the same spans, and the same `music.min_span_s` floor, that switch the bed), so the picture turns where the score does and a one-beat mood blip is not a section. Must be in `allowed`. Counts toward `animated_share`. Omitted means section changes get no special treatment.

durations.description: D95 — per-kind length, overriding `duration_s` for that kind: a dip to black wants longer than a crossfade. Same clamping as `duration_s`.

per_component.description: D95 slice 3 — the transition INTO the shot a given overlay opens on, by catalog component name: {"ChapterCard": "wipe"} makes every chapter card arrive on a wipe. Applies only when the overlay opens within 0.7 s after its shot starts — the compiler floors an overlay's start at 0.4 s into its beat — since an overlay that opens mid-shot has no cut to arrive on (the compile note says so). A beat's own transition_out still wins. Each kind must be in `allowed`. Counts toward `animated_share`. This is the SHOT transition; how the overlay itself animates in is the theme's `motion.per_component`.

script_persona.description: persona/style text for the script agent

visual_language.description: visual guidance text for the beat planner

script.description: narration shape (D45): length lives with the pacing numbers it interacts with, and is overridable per video like overlays.density

target_seconds.description: target seconds of speech; the script prompt receives it as {{target_seconds}}

tolerance.description: accepted deviation, as a fraction of target_seconds

prompt.description: prompt pack name carrying this pack's voice — layer 3 of the D44 resolution order

fallback.description: D55 — what to put on screen when the sources have nothing good enough (source_policy.visual.min_score_floor). A card that names the subject is honest; a clip that is nearly unrelated is a lie the viewer notices and cannot name. Absent = keep the weak asset, since a beat with nothing on it is worse than a beat with the wrong thing on it.

component.description: catalog component drawn over a plain colour fill; it must be one this pack's allowed_components list would accept

text_prop.description: which prop takes the words, derived from the beat's own keyword query (v1.1) or its visual_intent

sfx.description: D48 — how OFTEN sound effects fire. Numbers, enforced by the compiler and re-checked by the validator, exactly like overlays.density (D9). The theme picks which sound; this picks how many.

cues.description: which events may fire a cue at all. Transitions are opt-in on purpose.

max_per_minute.description: hard cap; the compiler drops the lowest-priority cues to stay under it

min_gap_s.description: minimum spacing between two cue starts; on collision the higher-priority cue survives

music.description: D48 — how background music is SHAPED across the video. Which bed comes from the theme's mood_beds; the mood itself comes from the beat sheet.

min_span_s.description: a mood run shorter than this merges into its neighbour. Without a floor, a two-beat mood blip restarts the bed and the score turns chatty.

crossfade_s.description: fade in/out at each span boundary; adjacent spans overlap by this much

one_bed.description: D114 — one bed under the whole video (Dark Palace), picked by the mood that covers the most time, fading in over 2.5 s and out over the last 5 s; false = a bed per mood span

duck.description: D114 — what the bed ducks against. sentences = the D48 envelope, lifting only in gaps of 1.2 s or more between sentence timings; waveform = Dark Palace's respiro: the voice's own waveform in 10 ms blocks (speech_windows.json), falling in 0.08 s when the narrator starts and rising in 0.6 s in every pause. waveform also crafts each bed (brought to -20 LUFS, its ends trimmed, looped through loop_crossfade_s seams to exactly its span), which is what lets the levels below be set in dB

under_voice_db.description: waveform only: the bed's loudness while the narrator speaks, in dB against the voice (mix.voice_lufs, else -14). Dark Palace: -28, its user's Premiere level for an ambience under a -14 LUFS voice

duck_db.description: waveform only: how far the bed rises in a pause (Dark Palace: 6)

hook_lift_db.description: waveform only: the bed sits this much higher through the hook and settles back over hook_settle_s after it (Dark Palace: 6). Needs pacing.hook

loop_crossfade_s.description: waveform only: the crafted bed's loop seam (Dark Palace: 7 s, equal-power)
